title: AI Maestro Board
description: Canonical schema for board/data.json. Epics group work; tickets are the unit of delivery and route themselves to an agent pipeline and a model tier.

traces_to.description: Plan item ids this epic delivers (D-/UC-/FR-/NFR-/M- from board/plan.json). An epic that traces to nothing is out of the plan's scope.

sample.description: Placeholder content seeded by a starter, not real work. `maestro ticket import --replace-sample` removes items carrying this flag, and only those — which is what makes replacing the starter board safe on a project that already has real tickets.

epicId.description: The epic this ticket belongs to.

desc.description: Short source of truth. Longer specs live in board/specs/<id>.md.

area.description: Part of the system (backend/frontend/infra/docs...). Sets area defaults like model floor and test command.

status.description: The last three are ARCHIVE-ONLY terminal states, for tickets that left the board without being completed — shelved pending an owner decision (archived), filed twice (duplicate), or deliberately declined (wont-do). Folding them into 'done' would record work as finished that never was. Live tickets in data.json may only use the first six; the validator errors otherwise.

depends_on.description: This ticket is eligible only when all referenced tickets are done.

agent_plan.description: Ordered pipeline of agent codes, e.g. ["pe","backend","qa","merge"]. Terminal gates (qa, pd, merge) are appended automatically if absent.

model.description: Baseline model tier. The ticket runs on the stronger of this and its area's model.floor. See docs/MODEL-ROUTING.md.

execution_mode.description: Shapes the pipeline: multi-agent runs the full gated pipeline (plan → implement → qa → pd → merge); single-agent runs a lighter path (one implementer → qa → merge).

wave.description: Optional ordering hint for batched runs.

agent.description: Human-readable display label (e.g. 'PE+QA'). Not used for execution — agent_plan is.

human_gate.description: When set, the orchestrator never auto-picks this ticket; a human must clear it. Value should come from the project's configured humanGates vocabulary.

failureKind.description: Optional, for blocker tickets created after a failed merge: classifies the structural failure mode so merge failures are queryable rather than free text. The validator warns on unknown values.

testCmd.description: Optional ticket-specific test command that overrides the area default in the release gate.

evidence.description: Verification evidence recorded when the ticket is completed (commit SHA, test output, etc.).

traces_to.description: Plan item ids this ticket serves (D-/UC-/FR-/NFR-/M- from board/plan.json). This is what the scope gate reads: a ticket tracing to nothing, to an id the plan doesn't define, or to an OUT- id is out of scope and the orchestrator refuses to pick it. See board/plan.schema.json.

touches.description: Glob patterns for the files this ticket is expected to change, e.g. ["src/api/**"]. Used only for PARALLEL scheduling: two tickets may share a lane or run in different ones, and declaring disjoint scopes is what lets them run at once. Undeclared is safe but pessimistic — the scheduler then falls back to epic, then area, and puts anything it cannot prove independent in the same lane. A ticket whose globs reach a serial-only file (migrations, lockfiles) runs alone.

sample.description: Placeholder content seeded by a starter, not real work. Removed by `maestro ticket import --replace-sample`.

scope_exception.description: A human's written reason for running this ticket despite being outside the plan. Clears the scope gate; still reported everywhere so the exception stays visible rather than becoming the norm.
